myths.title: Story of Valmiki and Hanuman
myths.text: One day Valmiki came to know that the great Hanuman too had penned the adventures of Rama, engraving the story with his nails on rocks. His curiosity was aroused and he traveled to the Himalayas where Hanuman was residing in order to see this version. The monkey warrior was no doubt an eyewitness to many of the incidents, but was he a poet? He questioned Hanuman about the rumor that he had composed his own Ramayana. Hanuman carried him and placed him on a ledge from which he could read the narration. Valmiki kept reading and reading, scanning the cliffs from top to bottom, climbing and descending now and again in order to see well. Sometimes he laughed loudly and at times his eyes brimmed with tears. Valmiki was overwhelmed by the sheer power and depth of devotion of the amazing narrative. It was truly a lofty work, inspired by great love. After finishing the story Valmiki gazed for a long time into the distance. Joy and sorrow flitted over his face. He was joyous at having had the chance to read such an exquisite work of art and sad because it obviously overshadowed his own work. Hanuman politely asked him the reason for his sorrow. “O best of sages! Is something wrong? Does the poetry have many faults?” Valmiki turned to him and said, “It is indeed a marvelous bit of work. Every image, every word is alive and pregnant with devotion. There is not and never can be an equal to it. My version, which I created with such pains over a period of twelve years, is no match for the magnificence of your work and will therefore be despised.” For a moment Hanuman was dumbstruck. Then he said, “Is that all that is bothering you?” He promptly tore the slabs on which he had scribbled the poem on the mountain and piled them on one shoulder. He placed the aged saint on another shoulder and flew to the ocean. When they reached the middle Hanuman called loudly, “May these be an offering to my Lord.” With these words, he threw his own version into the sea, where they raised huge waves before disappearing into the depths of the sea. Valmiki watched speechless, overcome with shame and guilt. “It would have been better,” he thought, “if he had thrown me into the sea and saved that wonderful story.” But Hanuman seemed unperturbed and cheerful. He returned the sage to his own hermitage in a trice. “Please don't worry about this,” he said. “It was just something I did to while away the time!” The Ramayana is a story of tyaga, or renunciation, and this aspect of Hanuman's personality is considered to be far more important than his rhetorical skills. Selfless and compassionate, his loyalty was always to his master and not to any particular telling of the tale, and he willingly drowned his own masterpiece in order to spare a poet's wounded pride. This was the first and greatest Ramayana, called the Hanumad Ramayana, which like the original Veda, was lost and preserved only in fragments. Hanuman bowed to Valmiki, who blessed him and said prophetically, “O Son of Vayu, in another age I will take birth again and devote myself to your service. I will sing your praises and teach others to do so. I will retell the story you have told, using the language of the common man so that everyone may understand it.” Hanuman smiled and said, “Victory to Lord Rama!”

key_points: The primary deity of this asterism, Vishvedevas have the power to grant unchallengeable victory over the evil. They deal with the laws of karma, right actions, the laws of time and universal moral principles. The ten deities control the various powers required for an individual to be well-rounded and successful. The ten qualities include Goodness, Truth, Will Power, Time, Desire, Skilfulness, Forbearance, Ancestors, Abundance, and Summit/ Peak. It is clear that all these ten gods are extremely benevolent and are representative of the primary virtues of the original, divine, and the creative spark. Uttara Ashadha hence represents all that is good and benign. It encompasses the qualities of all the previous constellations or predecessors:
Goodness with Ashwini, Punarvasu and Pushya
Truth with Uttara Phalguni
Will Power with Ardra and Krittika
Time with Bharani and Anuradha
Desire with Bharani, Rohini, Mrigashira and Ashlesha

myths.title: The Promise of the Sun God
myths.text: An interesting story is told that once an asura, who had pleased Brahma with his devotion, was granted a boon by the Creator of this universe, “Your life exists in the thousand kavachas (armours) that I have bestowed upon you and because of which none can kill you. But, if any one of your enemies were to remove the kavachas from your body, then you would lose all your powers. I also grant you another boon-one who takes away even one kavacha from you will have to fight you for a hundred years.” With such powerful boons granted to an asura, it was enough reason for this to go to his head. He began to exercise his powers for both good and evil purposes, as a result of which all came to dread him and gave him the name Sahasrakavacha (a hundred armours). The devas were so disgusted with his behaviour that they decided to approach Lord Vishnu to seek his intervention. On hearing their pleas, Lord Vishnu agreed to help them and descended on earth in the form of two men, named Nara and Narayana. Now these two men challenged Sahasrakavacha to a battle, which the asura willingly accepted, conscious as he was of his prowess and the hundred kavachas that he wore. The day of the battle arrived. Nara engaged Sahasrakavacha in the confrontation for a hundred years while Narayana sat down to do penance. After a hundred years, Nara managed to force one kavacha off from the asura's body by piercing through it and then embarked on penance. Meanwhile, Narayana took up the battle from where Nara had left. Thus alternating with each other, Nara and Narayana continued fighting with the asura, till he was left with only one kavacha upon his body. Now Sahasrakavacha realised that he was left with the last kavacha and if that too was ripped off his body, he would die. So, he went and hid himself behind the Sun-god. With Sahasrakavacha having left the field, Nara and Narayana returned to heaven. After a long time, a son was born to Kunti with the blessings of the Sun-god. The child was named Karna and he was born wearing a single kavacha upon himself. This evidently proved to the shocked people around him that Karna was none other than Sahasrakavacha who had taken rebirth as Karna. As we all know, in the battle of Mahabharata, Karna supported Duryo-dhana. Lord Indra disguised himself as a poor Brahmin and approached Karna for alms. Karna was a kind-hearted man, so he willingly took out his kavacha to hand over to the poor Brahmin. With the last kavacha off, Karna went to the battlefield and was killed by an arrow directed at him by Arjuna, who rode his chariot with Lord Krishna driving it. Arjuna and Krishna were Narayana and Nara respectively, in earlier life and were responsible for killing Karna. Thus, as promised by Brahma, Sahasrakavacha lived so long as he wore the kavachas.

ganesha.text: Dhundhi Ganapati is the 26th among the 32 forms of Lord Ganesha. This form of Ganapathi helps in attaining moksha through spiritual studies, thus making the devotees life fresh and glorious. He has a red-hued complexion and has four hands. In the upper right hand Dhundhi Ganapathi holds a japa beads mala (rudraksha) and in the lower right hand he holds his broken tusk. In the upper left hand he holds his axe and in the lower left hand he holds a pot of precious gems (Ratnakumbha). It is believed that the pot of precious gems represent the valuable box of alert or consciousness and a saver of faithful and loyal devotees.

key_points: Shravana means “the act of acquiring knowledge”. It comes from the root Sanskrit "Shru" which translates as “to hear”. It is common approach to acquire knowledge figuratively by listening so the literal meaning of Shravana is “acquiring knowledge by listening”. Hence this nakshatra is termed as “The Star of the Learning Ear”. Ear is a very straightforward symbol of this star.

Listening to “Silence” and the “Naada Brahma” (the eternal sound of the Universe also called God's Voice) reveals the beauty and harmony of the Cosmic Music. This nakshatra gives the capacity to the native to hear the astral sounds of Krishna's flute, and the celestial bells or the cosmic “Om”. This nakshatra has some association with the paramparas and Gurukul systems where there is Guru & Shishya type of relationship and Shastras are mastered by listening and serving the Guru.

Shravana's basic direction is towards the “Great Silence” which provides the background to survive the entire scheme of manifestation. Note that, Ear is the only sense organ of human beings which is most active when it is absolutely passive.

Vamana avatar of Vishnu spanned the universe (Earth, Heavens and Netherworld) in three steps denoting his expansive travels as taking command over the three worlds. This explains the three footprints symbology associated with this nakshatra. The restless nature of the Shravana natives causes them to travel extensively, usually in a pursuit of knowledge.

Since the footsteps symbolises walking and leaving an imprint, Shravana natives like hiking, cycling, running and traveling in general. If 9th Lord of 12th Lord is posited in Shravana nakshatra then the native might travel overseas and if 3rd Lord is placed here then it can indicate many short and frequent travels.

This nakshatra is considered as the birth star of Goddess Saraswathi. As the birth star of Saraswathi it signifies and bestows scholarship, educational proficiency, respect for the shastras, knowledge etc. The eminent men in the field of education and knowledge, the man who is listened to by others with respect is influenced by this star. Hence, Shravana nakshatra rules all kinds of oral communications and when focal planets are placed in this asterism tend to make the native talkative, effective speakers, as well as good listeners. They are gifted in delivering speeches and sermons in a rhythmic and melodically structured manner. They can make good news readers, masters of ceremonies, radio jockeys, etc.

Shravana natives have great capacity and thirst for knowledge, information and the rare ability to develop wisdom in life. They make great teachers, professional listeners or perpetual students. Counseling is a gift for they have the ability to truly listen. Their sense of hearing can be very acute and sensitive
Shravana natives may have keen interest in learning foreign languages.
The power of Shravana is “Samhanana Shakti” which gives the native the power to connect to higher levels of consciousness and it can lead the person to deep meditation.
Shravana natives are careful with their finances and may perform well as political campaign managers, advertising marketers, social historians, etc.
Male Shravana natives are kind hearted, very religious and generous in nature. Many social workers and philanthropists have Shravana rising in their charts.
Female Shravana natives are charitable and benevolent in nature. They can also make good designers and interior decorators.

myths.title: Vamana's Three Foot Steps
myths.text: The Bhagavata Purana describes that Vishnu descended as the Vamana avatar to restore the authority of Indra over the heavens, as it had been taken by Mahabali, a benevolent Asura King. Bali was the great grandson of Hiranyakshipu, the grand son of Prahlada and son of Virochana. Vamana, in the guise of a short Brahmin carrying a wooden umbrella, went to the king to request three paces of land. Mahabali consented, against the warning of his guru, Sukracharya. Vamana then revealed his identity and enlarged to gigantic proportions to stride over the three worlds. He stepped from heaven to earth with the first step, from earth to the netherworld with the second. King Mahabali, unable to fulfill his promise, offered his head for the third. Vamana then placed his foot and gave the king immortality for his humility. Mahabali is seen as a symbol of prosperity and love. In worshiping Mahabali and his ancestor Prahláda, he conceded sovereignty of Pátála, the netherworld. Some texts also report that Vamana did not step into the netherworld, and instead gave its rule to Bali. In giant form, Vamana is known as Trivikrama.

myths.title: Hidden Significance
myths.text: Mahabali symbolizes Samridhi means prosperity, the three feet symbolizes the three planes of existence (Jagrat, Swapna and Sushupti) and final step is on his head which elevates from all three states and he attains moksha.

nakshatras.meaning: “The Most Famous”, “The Swiftest”, “The Most Heard of”, “The Wealthiest”, “The Most Benevolent”, alternatively it is also called as "Shravishta”.
key_points: The root word of Dhanishtha comes from “Dhana” means Wealth and “Nistha” means Steady. The alternative meaning is “Dhwani” means Sound “Ishta” meaning Loving or Lover of Sound/ Music. Its also means a Steady Sound. . Its alternative name is "Shravishta", a Sanskrit term, which translates into "the Most Heard of" or "the Most Famous". The name Shravishta implies that Dhanishta forms a pair with the previous nakshatra Shravana.

Dhanishtha nakshatra as per the ancient texts was the start of the year in the Calendar of Vivaswaan Surya (father of Vaivaswat Manu) in Surya Siddhaant. This was during the times of Lord Karthikeya. That was the period of rains when the Sun was transiting in Dhanishtha nakshatra. Thus, the year started with Varshaa (Rains), so it was called Varsh.
The nakshatra consists of a small group of stars located in the head of Delhphonus, the Dolphin, Sadalsuud. It is good for intuitive ability, visionaries and for public relations.

The presiding deity of Dhanishtha are the Asta Vasus or the 8 Vasus: Apah (Water), Dhruva (Pole Star), Dhara (Earth), Anila (Wind), Soma (Moon), Anala/ Pavaka (Fire), Pratyusha (The Dawn), Prabhasa (Splendor). The Vasus are considered to be “Gods of Abundance”. They are the deities of the Earth that give abundance on the earthly plane. They are manifestations of Agni or the sacred fire and show the gifts that it can dispense. Because Vasus are the deity of this star - it is the giver of wealth, precious stones, valuable articles, gold, opulence etc.
The Shakti of Dhanishtha is called Khyapayitri Shakti which has the power to “Give Fame and Abundance”.
It is also called the "Star of Symphony"; there is considerable material wealth, ownership of property and real estate associated with this nakshatra.

The symbol of this nakshatra is the Drum or the Flute. Due to the symbols of musical instruments, some of the natives do possess musical ability and love dancing and keep to the rhythm and beat of the drums. In the same token they are great at timing; this can refer to having a knack for being at the right place at the right time.

The nakshatra planetary ruler is Mars. Mars is also Exalted at 28° Capricorn in the 2nd Pada of Dhanistha. The ruler of the Capricorn and Aquarius sign is Saturn and the nakshatra ruler Mars, both are Tamasic planets, which can give severe relationship issues to the native. Due the tamasic influence of Mars and Saturn this nakshatra is governed by the quality of “Tamas”.
It is considered a Rakshasa (Demonic) nakshatra. Once again, this can be attributed to its close relationship to the two natural malefics, Mars and Saturn.
It is a primarily "Pitta" (fiery) nakshatra due to its strong relation with the Pitta planet Mars.

The motivation in life of the nakshatra is “Dharma”, given it association with the righteous deities the Ashta Vasus and the association with the planet Saturn, who upholds Dharma. Note that Sri Krishna taught the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna on the battlefield (Mars) and reminded him of his Dharma to fight the war against his relatives.

The animal symbol of this nakshatra is the Lioness (Female Lion). This is associated to the power of Narasimhi (Half Lioness and Half Woman) the consort of Narasimha (The fierce Half-Lion and Half-Human form of Vishnu). She is one of the Asta Matrikas (8 Mother Goddesses) and is believed to have the power to throw the stars into disarray by shaking her lion mane. She was born to pacify and calm down the fierce form of Ugra Narasimha after he killed the demon Hiranyakashipu. This shows the fierceness of the Dhanishtha natives. They would typically need their partners/ spouses to be like Goddess Narasimhi who can calm them down from time to time.

The Life of Bheeshma, one of the major characters in the Vedic epic, "Mahabharata", exemplifies the functionings of Dhanishta. He took and observed the vow of lifelong celibacy and was unconquerable in battle; was generous even to his competitors and showed immaculate courage until his last breath.

myths.title: The Story of Dhruva
myths.text: Dhruva was born a son of the King Uttānapāda (the son of Svayambhuva Manu) and his wife Suniti. The king also had another son Uttama, born to his second queen Suruchi, who was the preferred object of his affection. Once, when Dhruva was a child of five years of age, he was sitting on his father's lap at the King's throne. Suruchi, who was jealous of the older son from the first wife (since he – Dhruva – would be heir to throne, and not Suruchi's son), forcefully removed Dhruva from his father's lap. When Dhruva protested and asked if he could not be allowed to sit on his father's lap, Suruchi berated him saying, 'only God can allow you that privilege. Go ask him.' Suniti – being of gentle nature and now the lesser favorite wife – tried to console the distraught child, but Dhruv was determined to hear of his fate from the Lord himself! Seeing his firm resolve, his mother bade him farewell as he set out on a lonely journey to the forest. Dhruva was determined to seek for himself his rightful place, and noticing this resolve, the divine sage Narada appeared before him and tried to desist him from assuming a severe austerity upon himself at such an early age. But, Dhruv's fierce determination knew no bounds, and the astonished sage guided him towards his goal by teaching him the rituals and mantras to meditate on when seeking lord Vishnu. The one mantra which Narada taught and which was effectively used by Dhruv was Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya. Having been advised, Dhruv started his meditation, and went without food and water for six months, his mind fixed on the Lord. The austerity of his tapasya shook the heavens and the Lord appeared before him, but the child would not open his eyes because he was still merged in his inner vision of Vishnu's form described to him by Narada. Lord Vishnu had to adopt a strategy of causing that inner vision to disappear. Immediately Dhruva opened his eyes, and, seeing outside what he had been seeing all along in his mental vision, prostrated himself before the Lord. But he could not utter a single word . The Lord touched his right cheek by his divine conch and that sparked off his speech. Out poured forth a beautiful poem of praise of the Lord in 12 powerful verses, which together are called Dhruva-stuti. Vishnu Purana gives a slightly different account here. When Vishnu was pleased with Dhruva's tapasya and asked him to ask for a varadān (grant of wishes), Dhruv said that he (being an uneducated child) did not know how to sing the praise of Lord Vishnu, and therefore asked the varadān of a knowledge of stuti (hymn in the praise of Vishnu). Other persons would have asked for worldly or heavenly pleasures, or for moksha at most, but Dhruva had no personal desire. Renunciation of all desires is regarded to be essential for eternal peace in Hinduism: this is the meaning of Dhruva-pada. That was the reason why the Saptarshis decided to give Dhruva the most revered seat of a Star. The Dhruva-stuti as mentioned in the Vishnu Purana is an extended version of the Vedic Purusha sukta and is quite different from the Dhruva-stuti of Bhagavata Purana. Having spent a long time in the Lord's remembrance he even forgot the objective of his tapasya, and only asked for a life in memory of the Lord. Pleased by his tapasya and by his stuti, Vishnu granted his wish and further declared that the lad would attain Dhruvapada – the state where he would become a celestial body which would not even be touched by the Maha Pralaya, or the final destruction. Dhruva returned to his kingdom, to be warmly received by his family, and attained the crown at the age of six. He ruled for many decades in a fair and justice manner. This story reiterates the determination that is associated with Dhanishta.

nakshatras.meaning: Requiring a Hundred Physicians or Hundred Healers.
key_points: The root word of Shatabhisha is “Shatabhisaj” which transalates as Shata - Hundred + Bhishaj – Healer or a Cure. Note the shakti of this nakshatra is called Bheshaja Shakti which is the Power to “Heal and Support”

This nakshatra is a large group of faint stars (approx. 100) in the sign of the Water Bearer (Aquarius). The water poured out of this pot is the nectar or the elixir of immortality. The Fomalhaut is a star of musical abilities and great spirituality. It can be very treacherous or very benefic.

The image of this nakshatra depicts the Solar deity (one of the 12 Adityas) Varuna holding a pot in one hand. This pot contains Soma - the preferred drink of the Gods or the elixir of life. Soma is the heavenly ambrosia which suggests the idea of rejuvenation (magical cures through this divine water) and intoxication. In the other hand Varuna is seen holding some medicinal herbs. This is where the hundred physicians come into the picture.

Varuna is the presiding deity of this nakshatra. The word Varuna literally means, “The All Enveloping Sky” or “The Binder” or “The Coverer”. The symbol of this nakshatra is the “Empty Circle” which is an image of the all-encompassing sky. Hence Shatabisha is the star which promotes aeronautics, out space explorations and other atmospheric endeavors. It is the star associated with western civilization and has a significant role in the technological development of humanity.

Varuna rules the invisible and is hence the God of the Underground Waters. He is the Chief of the 12 Adityas. He rules magical powers and is the Lord of destiny and rules over the West. He rules over law and the underworld. Varuna has extraordinary power to heal through his magical herbs and medicine.

The circle symbol attributed to this nakshatra shows the independent, contained nature of the native with a strong desire for seclusion and solitude. The empty circle also represents things that are hidden and mysterious. Hence people with prominent planets here may have interest in esoteric and occult subjects such as astrology, holistic sciences, pranic healing, modern research in technology, etc. The empty circle also symbolizes holding or containing things and can signify the concealed knowledge or vidya. The hidden amrita (ambrosia) in the Khumbha (The Pot) which is not for everyone.

Varuna is considered as the God the Dark Sky. The stars in the night sky are considered to be the eyes of Varuna, through which he is believed to watch the hidden affairs of humans and arrest the deceitful with his divine noose. The noose also signifies the empty circle symbol of this nakshatra. Ketu placed in this nakshatra may result in death through hanging or suicide for the relative signified by the house occupied in the native's chart. Hence Shatabhisha is a star of justice and fair treatment, punishing whomever deserves punishment, without considering their status. Hence this is a star of revolutionary movement and liberal forces in human society (traits strongly observed in Western Civilizations).

Varuna is also connected to the movement of the Sun in the southern hemisphere which is called Dakshinayana. The lower lower half of the Universe is called “Underworld” and Varuna has his dominion over this region similar to Indra who rules over the Heavens or Swarga Loka. As a result Shatabhisha controls counter-culturism and underground movement of social groups.

Varuna being the Lord of the underworld has great control over affairs of death. Also, since he is God of Celestial Water and Nectar, he also has the ability to give Life. Hence in Rig Veda he is called the “God of Immortality”, since he holds the power of Life and Death. Hence illness in Shatabhisha is very difficult to cure and the symbolically the native may have to go 100 physicians or healers and may find it difficult to get a suitable remedy. It may bring about a healing crisis to the native, going from one doctor to another with not much result. Such people should go to a Ashwini nakshatra healers to get immediate cure.
Varuna is also the God of Sin, Debts, Injury and Disease, who not only brings these calamities upon us but can remove them from us, if we propitiate him sincerely.

The nakshatra deity Varuna also has the power to protect and maintain the natural and moral laws of nature. He represents the vital connection between the Gods and Humanity and hence gives the natives the ability to counter difficult karmas through divine grace, repentance, and sustained effort requiring longer period of time.

Also known as the 'The Veiling Star' which brings secretiveness and keeping certain aspects of self from the public view.

The ocean, rivers, lakes, etc are derived from this star and it signifies aquatic marine life. It concerns boats, concealment, the veil, and to hide beneath the veil, covering, armour, places to hide things, failures, no-easy success, sorrow, restraint, idleness, peevishness, cynicism and a mania for excessive cleanliness. myths.title: The Story of Varuna's Cow
myths.text: Sage Kashyapa once prepared to perform a great sacrifice. All arrangements were complete but he could not procure a suitable cow for the Yajna. So he stole a cow, Kamadhenu, from the cattle-shed of Varuna. Aditi and Surasaa, his two wives, concealed the cow in the Ashrama as the sage started performing the Yajna. When Varuna came to know of the theft of his heavenly cow, he went to sage Kashyapa and demanded it. Kashyapa was not inclined to return it. Varuna was annoyed and cursed his own father: “May you be born as a human being on Earth and tend the cows, you who have stolen my lovely cow. Both your wives would be born there too. The calves of my cow are in distress without their mother. As a consequence, Aditi would suffer confinement as well as loss of her children.” After that, Varuna went to lord Brahma and said to him: “Lord! What should I do? My cow has been stolen by sage Kashyapa who refuses to return her despite my entreaties. So I have pronounced a curse upon him.” Lord Brahma summoned sage Kashyapa and addressed him thus: “Noble sage, why don't you return the cow to Varuna? You are wise and learned. There is nothing that is not known to you. How could you stoop to this lowly act? You have succumbed to greed which is a certain path to hell. Greed, the greatest enemy of man, robs a man of his piety. Greed has led you, O' sage, to this fallen state.” Saying thus, lord Brahma too cursed sage Kashyapa: “Be born, through a fraction of your being, as an earthling along with your two wives, and serve there as a cowherd.” Sage Kashyapa incarnated on Earth as Vasudeva. His wives Aditi and Surasaa were born as Devaki and Rohini respectively, the mothers of Krishna and Balarama.

Shatabhisha's symbol is an empty circle and its deity is Varuna, the Vedic god of cosmic and terrestrial waters. The circle suggests separation and containment, in its circumference dividing space into inner and outer. The circumferential fence simultaneously protects the inner being from any outer danger and prevents it from joining the greater whole by segregating it, holding it captive. A shoreline confines a body of water in the same way that horizon, the limit of our vision, encloses the sky. Shatabhisha rules reservoirs, tanks, lakes, armour, and shields outer garment and cloaks. Shatabhisha is commonly assumed to cloak or veil things, to keep them hidden, secret. This asterism also traps and paralysis, both literal and symbolic. myths.text: Purva Bhadrapada - Sacred Animal Lion - The Story of Lord Narasimha and Prahlad. Hiranyaksha & Hiranyakashipu were brothers – and Lord Vishnu in his Varaha Avatar would kill Hiranyaksha. To take revenge his brother Hiranyakashipu performed severe penance and attained a boon from Brahma – The creator. That he would not die either on earth or in space; nor in fire nor in water; neither during day nor at night; neither inside nor outside (of a home); nor by a human, animal or God; neither by inanimate nor by animate being. With virtually no fear of death he unleashes terror. Hiranyakashipu declares himself as god and asks people not to utter god's name except his. However his son Prahlada (who is a devoted worshiper of Lord Vishnu!) refuses. Repeated pressurization on him yields no results for Hiranyakashipu. Prahlada declares the omnipresence of Lord Vishnu. One day Hiranyakashipu points to a pillar and asks if Vishnu is present in it. Prahlada said “Yes!”. His father becomes furious and draws his sword and cuts the pillar; Narasimha(The avatar of vishnu) appears out of the broken pillar. Narasimha (being a man-lion god form) kills Hiranyakashipu. He comes out to kill at the twilight (neither day nor night);on the doorsteps of his palace (neither inside nor outside); uses his nails to kill (neither animate nor inanimate); puts him on his lap before killing (neither earth nor in space). Thus making the power of the boon ineffective. The specific purpose of this avatar was for protection of his devotee Prahlada from his demon father Hiranyakashipu, to prove a point and to make true the words of his devotee that God is in existence everywhere. Prahlada's episode proves that God will always come to the rescue of his devotees who Prays him with sincere devotion.

nakshatras.root: Uttara = latter; Bhadra = blessed, happy, fortunate; Pada = foot.
nakshatras.meaning: “The Second of the Blessed Feet”, “The Beautiful Left Foot”, or a “Ray of Light”.
key_points: Uttara Bhadrapada" translates into - "the latter (one who possesses) lucky feet". Its alternative name is "Uttaraproshthapada", which translates into "the latter (one who possesses) the feet of a stool”.
The symbol is the "back part of a funeral cot'. A funeral cot denotes our exit from the world. Moreover, it lies completely in the Pisces, the 12H of exit of the natural zodiac.
The alternative symbol for this Nakshatra is the twins, which reflect the duality and opposite, yet interconnected, influences upon those with natal Moon in Uttara Bhadrapada.

Uttara Bhadrapada lies entirely in Pisces, which is ruled by auspicious and expansive Jupiter, however Uttara Bhadrapada itself is ruled by restrictive and passive Saturn. Like with its counterpart Purva Bhadrapada, though challenging, these contrary energies, when brought together can bring about great transformation in the individual. This duality of both contrast and harmony is also reinforced by this Nakshatra's Guna qualities – Sattwic on the one hand and Tamasic on the other hand. Though the Sattwic quality is dominant, the main motivation, or Purushartha, is towards Kama, which has a Tamasic tendency. Note that the Kama of this nakshatra is not the sexual passion but the intense desire to merge with the universal consciousness.

It is called as the "Warrior Star", and the native are disciplined with writing and speaking abilities. Note that the caste of this nakshatra is Kshatriya (Warrior). They are somewhat like the former nakshatra Purva Bhadrapada but a lot milder, and can control their anger and aggression.
The natives acquire wealth usually as a gift or inheritance, usually latter in life. They are cheerful, generous, and self sacrificing.

The presiding deity is Ahir Budhyana the serpent of the deep waters representing kundalini energy, seclusion and psychic energy. A serpent or snake also symbolizes wisdom, concealed knowledge, growth cycles, and rebirth. He is the son of Viswakarma (The Celestial Architect) and is one of the 11 Rudras. He is associated with Deep Water and Darkness. He represents the merging of consciousness with the universal consciousness. Those under the influence of this Nakshatra will be drawn towards expanding their consciousness and understanding the hidden wisdom of the psyche, the soul, and the Universe.
Uttara Bhadrapada is associated with Navami (9th tithi) of the waxing and waning phases of the Moon's monthly cycle.

The animal symbol of this nakshatra is a Cow, which indicates a docile and passive sexual nature. It is not a very sexually active nakshatra. It however can be quite interested in sex from a tantra point of view. The Cow is a sacred animal in India and this suggests the honor and respect that Uttara Bhadrapada can command.

Uttara Bhadrapada grants growth and prosperity in a broad way, benefiting the entire world. This makes it very auspicious. Ahir Budhyana is the benefic serpent who brings the rain, connecting us with the creative powers at the foundations of the world.
Anthropomorphically the sole of the feet of Kalapurush is connected to this nakshatra.

myths.title: The Story of Goddess Lakshmi, Lord Shani and Sage Narada
myths.text: Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Shani (saturn) met each other at an event. While they were talking to each other. Lord Shani said - “I am greater than you, as i am uphold dharma in the world. I stand for righteousness”. Goddess Lakshmi was furious she replied - “I am greater than you as i bring fortune, wealth and prosperity to the world”. Lord Shani argued - “You do not stay with one person for a long time, you do not have the power of discrimination as sometimes you can also stay with an evil minded person.” Goddess Lakshmi replied - “Whatever it is people invite me and offer prayers to get my blessings, but everyone is afraid of you and they pray for you to leave them.” Lord Shani said - “When you go into the wrong hands, it becomes my responsibility to correct them. You create maya in people's live while my duty is to expel the maya and make them face the truth/reality.” Goddess Lakshmi said - “Let's ask Lord Brahma”. Lord Shani agreed and they went to Lord Brahma and asked him to decide who is greater among them. Lord Brahma thought about the consequence of picking an answer and diplomatically pointed them towards Lord Vishnu. When they went to Lord Vishnu with the same question he pointed them towards the wise Sage Narada. Finally they asked Sage Narada to decide. After dodging them with a lot of playful naughtiness, the Sage answered thus. “Both of you are great! Equally great! Goddess Lakshmi you are great when you walk towards someone, and you are not so great when you walk away from someone. Lord Shani you are great when you walk away from someone and not so great when you walk towards someone. So in my honest opinion both of you are great. You both are there to help man reach his final goal of salvation. Either with the contentment of having enough of the material gains a person turns towards self exploration or after realizing the emptiness in the material wealth a person starts to question the true purpose of life and in some cases out of utter helplessness people turn towards God and Spirituality.” Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Shani were happy with the answer and walked away happily! And that brought a sigh of relief to Sage Narada. This story has a lot of significance to Uttara Bhadrapad nakshatra. Goddess Lakshmi is associated with this nakshatra and Lord Shani rules this nakshatra. So with time these natives turn towards the final goal of enlightenment and emancipation.

themes: Uttara Bhadrapada can be deep thinkers and may have a tendency to be agonized about the functioning of the world and take it in their stride.

Here the native have a controlled emotions and life patterns since the deity is the deep water serpent Ahir Budhyana. This traits may make them renunciates who are more happy being in a meditative and serene state like the hermits, sanyasis, etc.

Uttara Bhadrapada signifies the deep sleep state, in which the dream state is at its minimum, and we go to the depths of our unconsciousness. This nakshatra is also associated with the Kundalini serpant energy, the primeval life force that lies at the base of the spine in humans. Anuradha nakshatra is the initiator of awakening the Kundalini energy and Uttara Bhadrapada is the culmination point of this process.

The primary deity Ahir Budhyana is considered to the associated with maintaining the fertility of the earth. It is considered to be lying in the depth of Mother Earth and giving it Structure and Fertility. Hence this nakshatra is also associated with agriculture and dissolution of the Earth (Pralaya).

It is a Dhruva/ Fixed nakshatra as is quiet determined to achieve its set goals and is compared to a wise old man or the elder tribal leader who never acts hastily, and plans his actions after giving due consideration to his experiences from the past. In some circumstances it is seen nakshatra delays actions for too long for it own good, which is the trait due to its influence of the Saturnian energy. And just like the Tamasic qualities of Saturn in some cases they may be lazy in both physical and mental matters.
Uttara Bhadrapada natives can make very good counsellors. The cooling water of this nakshatra has the ability to extinguish the fire and the fiery emotions like anger, revenge and jealousy.
The calculative and mental stability of this nakshatra gives the ability to be connected with occult sciences such as astrology, numerology, yoga, meditation, and divination, etc.
Natives born under the strong influence of this nakshatra usually benefit from gifts, donations, and inheritances, etc.
This nakshatra has strong secretive and reclusive tendencies which may make them prematurely retire from their worldly duties.
The natives may have a neglected childhood and normally subject to life away from their town of birth.
The natives of this nakshatra are interested in fine arts and have the ability to write prolonged articles or books.
Natives with their focal planets in this nakshatra can be selfless, generous, have a liking for the oceans or deep sea explorations, have good children and live a righteous lives.

This nakshatra may bless the native with inspiration and imagination on one side but it may also cause sadness and depression. However, Uttara Bhadrapada is quiet strong on the face not to display their discomfort and inner grief in public. They have the ability to go through toughest periods of their lives with patience and calmness.Their ultimate destination is to find a foundation, which transcends the emotional ups and downs of life. That foundation is the ocean of pure universal consciousness which is realized when the Kundalini is finally awakened.

nakshatras.root: Revat = wealthy, rich, prosperous, abundant, plentifull, beautiful, splendid.
nakshatras.meaning: “One who Nourishes bringing Growth and Prosperity”, Revati means the “Shining One” or the “Shining Light” who shows the Path to Others. Revati Rescues those Who Deserve Special Protection, such as Children and Animals.
key_points: The root word describing Revati, is Ru which means: “She who increases prosperity, success, fortune, wealth, and abundance”
Goddess Revati is the daughter of King Kakudmi or Aivata who ruled Kusasthali, a kingdom beneath the ocean. Kakudmi was the descendant of Suryavansha or the Solar Dynasty and the son of King Revata

Revati is the wife of Balarama, elder brother of Lord Krishna as per mythology. Symbolically the tale of Devaki, Rohini and Balarama (refer Mythology section of Revati) leads us to the secret energy inherent in this nakshatra i.e., “Mysterious Preservation” and “Protective Principle” and gives the angle of “Surrogacy” and “Foster Parenting” in this asterism

'A Pair of Fish' is a symbol of deep spirituality and signifies the merging of the 'Jivatman' (the individual soul) with the 'Paramatman' the (Universal soul). The fish also gives fertility and allows for rapid growth

'The Drum' is a marker of time and indicator of the good sense rhythm it can bring to one's life. Hence, this constellation is related to time and other kinds of rhythmic measurements or activities such as Music, and should ensure timely sleep, exercise, and eating in their lives

Pushan the deity of Revati is invoked for the “Protection of Flocks and Herds” and for “Safe Travel”. Revati natives have been known to be giving foster care to others children or animals. They have and affinity or love towards small domestic animals.
The name Pushan comes from the Sanskrit verb 'Pusyati', which means “one who cause people to thrive, one who brings bliss and prosperity”

Pushan is also the “Ruler of the Roads” and is conducive nakshatra to commence your journeys. He has his rulership over streetlights and lighthouses which help ships from getting lost. This nakshatra may also indicate our final journey from life to the next
Pushan is the Ferryman who yearns to cross over the dead through river Vaitarani which falls on the Southern gate of the infernal city of Naraka (Garuda Purana), the realm of Yama (God of the Dead)

Since the deity Pushan ushers the dead souls to the realm of Yama, it is seen that this asterism gives prominence to hospice workers. Revati natives have a generous and a protective spirit and is willing to give nourishment and sustenance to the people on the streets

Pushan is also the Lord of lost things or lost animals and also considered the healer of the animals. 6L placed with no afflictions in Revati can give a liking to pet animals. However, multiple malefic influences can sometimes create the fear of animals or problems due to animals
Since Revati is a Tiryanga Mukha nakshatra, projects that commence in this asterism progresses sequentially without any hurdles
Revati is one of the most benefic nakshatras for spiritual growth and development of psychic abilities

The animal symbol of Revati is the Elephant, which usually likes to roam on level than on uneven terrain this explains the balanced and level nature of the asterism. Like the symbol Elephant the natives are probe to fatness and superfluity

Revati's influence enables its beneficiaries to do great service for their fellow beings without expecting much in return and the impulses flowing through this asterism leads to expansion of awareness
Revati natives are known to be weak in their childhood and are usually seen to be prone to frequent illnesses
Revati being a constellation placed in the watery sign of Pisces, it is seen that such native has love for water and benefit from living by the water
Out of all the 27 Nakshatra born persons, Revati born persons are the most god fearing and are religiously much inclined
Revati born are observed to be mostly settled in foreign countries or reasonably far from their places of birth. Also, the Revati native cannot stick to any particular field of work or job for long

Revati likes to guide and rescue those who deserve special protection: such as children and animals and are often seen in paediatrics, veterinary medicine, hospice work, emergency response, animal activism and protective shelters. It is often seen that such natives make good adoptive parents (foster fathers and mothers)
The destructive and dissolute power of the universe to create the Mahapralaya is the state and process which operates under Revati's energy

The planet Venus is exalted in the last quarter of this mercurial constellation (at 27 degrees in Pisces, the 12th sign of the natural zodiac showing Venus's importance in final liberation or moksha), and mythologically the planet Saturn is born in this nakshatra. However, the last quarter of Revati considered inauspicious for longevity
Anthropomorphically this is the cavity of the abdomen, groins of Kalapurusha

According to Varahamihira, Moon in Revati “gives one perfect body and physical felicity. The native is supposed to be blessed with purity, luck, wealth and a heroic disposition.” One will generally find that those having Moon or Ascendant in Revati are usually gentle, kind and pious unless there are other overwhelming factors to the contrary in the chart.

animal.name: Female Elephant
animal.text: Female Elephant & Leadership An elephant herd usually comprises six to twelve elephants, and is led by the wisest and oldest female, known as the “matriarch.” The herd relies on her to lead and make decisions regarding the course of action. The herd follows the matriarch by walking behind her in single file. Young elephants follow their mothers, holding onto their tails by their little trunks. The characteristics of the elephant alpha-female represent true and effective leadership: she is a role model. Because of size, she doesn't have the speed of other powerful animals. She makes up for it with her leadership skill set, which enables elephants to survive their harsh environment, unique in the animal kingdom.

myths.title: The Story of Pushan's Teeth
myths.text: According to a narrative found in the Taittiriya Samhita, Rudra was excluded from the Daksha yajna, an important sacrifice in honor of various deities. He, in anger, pierced the sacrifice with an arrow and Pushan broke his teeth as he attempted to eat a part of the oblation. The later versions of this narrative are found in the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and the Puranas. In these versions, Rudra (or Shiva) was angry because his father-in-law, Daksha, the sacrificer, did not invite him. Shiva, in anger, kicked Pushan and knocked out his teeth as he was eating the oblation. In the Puranic versions, Virabhadra, created by Shiva from a lock of his matted hair, knocked down Pushan's teeth.

ganesha.text: Sankatahara Ganapati is the final among the 32 forms of Lord Ganesha. The lord “Sankatahara” literally means “dispeller of all sorrow”. In this form Ganapathi appears seated on red lotus with his consort Sakthi (Devi) seated on his left thigh dressed in green attire and she holds lotus flower. The complexion of Sankatahara Ganapati is like sunshine hue and dressed in blue attire with four hands. His main right hand postures Varadha Mudra rewarding wishes to his devotees and his main left arm gently holds around Goddess Sakthi and holds the vessel of sweet milk pudding.

abhijit.name: Abhijit
text: The sidereal orbital period of the Moon takes around 27.323 days. A sidereal day is 23 hours 56 minutes and 4.1 seconds. The balance of 0.323 days which equates to 7 hours and 38 minutes of the sidereal day was considered to be associated with Abhijit Nakshatra which equals to the zodiacal span of 4° 14' 15'. The stellar sidereal zodiac of Abhijit corresponds to 6°40' - 10° 53' 20'' Capricorn or extends from the last pada (quarter) of Uttara Ashadha Nakshatra and it extends up to 1/15th part of Shravana Nakshatra in the equal 27 nakshatra system. Abhijit is associated with the star Vega (Alpha Lyrae). This is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

Abhijit means "Ultimate Victory" or "the One who cannot be defeated". This description also appropriately comes from the inherent power associated with Uttara Ashada Nakshatra "Apradhrishya Shakti" which translates as the power to Give an unstoppable or Permanent Victory. This makes logical sense, as a major portion of this nakshatra falls under the remit of Uttara Ashada Nakshatra in the 27 equal division system of nakshatras.

In some puranic context, the 27 Nakshatras were considered as the wives of the Moon God and hence some scholars believe that each of the 27 asterisms is feminine, and only Abhijit Naskshatra is masculine, and hence also be associated with Lord Vishnu since a portion of this falls in the Nakshatra of Shravana. In Bhagavad Geeta, Krishna tells Arjun, that among Nakshtras he is Abhijit, which remarks the auspiciousness of the Nakshatra and also underlines the importance of Abhijit. Vidhaata/Brahma (Universal Creator and Craftsman) is considered by many schools of nakshatra astrology to be the principal deity (tutelary archetype) of this nakshatra.

Currently, Abhijit is considered as an intercalary nakshatra and falls outside the scope of the 27 nakshatra mandala scheme, and is currently used in Muhurta/ Prashna Shastra (Electional Astrology). Classical vedic texts mention Abhijit (differently associated from the Nakshatra) as one of the most auspicious times for commencing important activity except travel in the southern direction. Many panchangams (Indian Ephemeris) give details of 28 minutes before and 28 minutes after 12:00 clock (a.m. and p.m. both) and call this time Abhijit Muhurta.
